rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe’s precise order and provision show that God alone is worthy of worship and governs its affairs.
rows.anchor: the reason that this whole universe is based on such a meticulous and punctual system

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that any partners in governance would disrupt the universe, as 21:22 also states.
rows.anchor: then this whole system would have aborted as is mentioned elsewhere in the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities worshipped besides God are fabrications.
rows.anchor: all these deities that these people worship are fabrications

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe witnesses both God’s oneness and His exalted greatness; the day and night and the subservient sun and moon show how far He is above partners.
rows.anchor: the system of this universe bears witness to the oneness of God, it also indicates that exalted and great is the person of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship example urges patience in trials and gratitude for blessings, the path to peace and success.
rows.anchor: they should show patience in this trial and express gratitude on their blessings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People grow arrogant in ease, briefly repent when seized by hardship, then return to their wrongdoing once comfort resumes.
rows.anchor: As soon as life becomes comfortable for them, they will return to their ill-ways.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In calm seas, passengers credit their own skill and intelligence rather than God’s provision of favorable winds.
rows.anchor: its passengers do not even think that it is because God has provided it with propitious winds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once ashore, few keep their promise to obey God; most become rebellious and ungrateful, forget His signs, and return to their former errors.
rows.anchor: very few of them adhere to their promise and adopt the middle path. Most of them turn out to be rebellious and ungrateful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the description of some passengers as moderate, an omitted phrase meaning that most are unbelievers is supplied by the later wording.
rows.anchor: This suppression is unfolded by the later words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqtasid refers to people who follow the path of truth and justice.
rows.anchor: The word ٌدِصَتۡقُّم refers to those who tread the path of truth and justice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khattār is an intensive form and denotes extreme unfaithfulness and the most heinous breaking of promises.
rows.anchor: It means someone who is unfaithful to the utmost and breaches promises in the most heinous way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khattār contrasts with sabbār: the latter stays true to God in every circumstance, while the former ignores Him in ease and remembers Him only during trials.
rows.anchor: The word ارَّبَص refers to people who remain steadfast on their covenant with God in all circumstances

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This pattern is an especially grave rebellion; neither God’s signs of favor nor warnings affect such people.
rows.anchor: For such people, neither signs of God’s favours nor any warning is effective.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Judgment Day, neither father nor child can help the other; each bears their own burden, and even the closest bond cannot change this.
rows.anchor: the day on which neither a father will be of any benefit to his children nor a son will be of any avail to his father

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the subject and using a noun instead of a verb strongly emphasizes the denial of benefit.
rows.anchor: the repetition of the inchoative ( mubtadā’) and use of a noun in place of the verb has added a lot of stress in the sentence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis is heightened because fathers naturally expect sons to support them, sons are better able to aid frail fathers, and young sons have stronger feelings of honor and civility.
rows.anchor: such will be the situation of indifference on that day that a son will not be able to be of any benefit to his father

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes fathers who forcibly opposed their sons’ Islam, claiming they would answer to God for their sons’ deeds.
rows.anchor: in those times fathers would forcibly stop their sons from accepting Islam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because worldly life is a test rather than a system of immediate reward and punishment, evil people may appear successful; this should not undermine belief in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: This world is not based on the principle of reward and punishment and since good and evil both have been given respite in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly deception must not lead people to think that God created without purpose or ignores good and evil; complete justice will ultimately appear and bring regret to the deluded.
rows.anchor: this deceptive state of affairs should not lure people into any misconception about God that He has made this world without a purpose

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects this warning to 82:6, which asks what deceived a person about the Beneficent Lord.
rows.anchor: In Sūrah Infiṭār, the words used to convey this very meaning are

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghurūr can mean the deceptive world or Satan; these are the two deceptions, worldly life and false notions about God, underlying deviations from truth.
rows.anchor: these are the two deceptions which are the foundation of all deviations from the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In answer to opponents asking when Judgment will come, he says only God knows its time; ignorance of timing does not negate that it will happen.
rows.anchor: Only He knows when the Day of Judgement will come; yet it is sure to come.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even carefully laid individual plans can fail just as they are about to materialize.
rows.anchor: just as it is about to materialize a calamity strikes and ruins the whole program.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Governments plan carefully for future crops, but weather and rain can disrupt those plans.
rows.anchor: What to speak of individuals, even governments plan with great care and confidence regarding the crops they will be producing the following year

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may be born in one place, live in another, and die in a third.
rows.anchor: At one place he is born, at another he lives and at still another place he dies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may leave home happily and return only as a corpse, illustrating how unpredictably death can intervene.
rows.anchor: Many a time a person merrily leaves his house with only his corpse to return.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even careful individual and government plans for future crops can be upset by weather and rain.
rows.anchor: change in weather conditions and rain disrupts their whole planning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People do not know where they will die or be buried; they may leave home happily and return only as a corpse, living and dying in different places.
rows.anchor: who knows in which land he will die and where he will be buried.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people cannot know even these undeniable nearby realities, ignorance of Judgment’s timing cannot make it doubtful.
rows.anchor: how can the Day of Judgement become dubious if its time of arrival is not known?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone truly knows and is cognizant; although only He knows Judgment’s timing, it is certain, and every particle of the universe testifies to its coming.
rows.anchor: Only He knows when the Day of Judgement will come; yet it is sure to come.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah Sajdah is the counterpart of Sūrah Luqmān: they share the central theme, the name Alif Lām Mīm, and similar introductions.
rows.anchor: This sūrah is the counterpart of Sūrah Luqmān, the previous sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation of the Qur’an was a great favor to the unlettered Arabs, who had not previously received a warner, and they should value it with gratitude.
rows.anchor: By revealing it to the unlettered Arabs, the Almighty has done a great favour to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the Qur’an is fabricated is false: it is certainly God’s truth, sent to warn people and guide them; if they devalue it, they face the fate of earlier nations.
rows.anchor: there is not the slightest doubt in it being the Book of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse next validates Qur’anic claims that especially alarmed its opponents.
rows.anchor: the discourse proceeds to validate the claims of the Qur’ān which were specially causing alarm in the minds of the opponents

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the sūra’s end, the Torah is cited as a comparable book revealed to Moses, which Pharaoh and his people opposed and whose opposition ended badly.
rows.anchor: a book similar to the Qur’ān was revealed to Moses (sws) which was opposed by the Pharaoh and his people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad and his followers, like the bearers of the Torah, must pass tests of patience; if they succeed, they will win and their opponents will be humiliated.
rows.anchor: the ultimate victory will be theirs and his opponents will be humiliated

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summary of verses 4–9 says the world is no amusement and that God made it in an elaborate manner.
rows.anchor: It is stated that this world is not a place of amusement. The Almighty has made it in a very elaborate manner
